claims.text: Nvidia is raising prices on AI hardware built on its Grace Blackwell 300 and Vera Rubin 200 chip generations
claims.reasoning: Both Bloomberg (fetched via Fortune's same-byline republication after Bloomberg's own URL returned HTTP 403) and The Information (headline/byline confirmed) name these two chip generations as the ones affected. Two independent sources with distinct attribution chains.

claims.text: Bloomberg reported the increase at more than 15%; The Information separately reported it at about 17%, citing server makers passing the increase on to customers
claims.reasoning: Verifier confirmed both figures from each outlet's own headline/text rather than a secondary summary. The two figures are close but not identical and come with different attribution (Nvidia-to-customers vs. server-maker-to-customers) -- exactly what the independence rule requires to count as two sources rather than one relayed number. Both figures are reported rather than collapsed into one invented precise number.

claims.text: The new pricing applies to systems shipping from early 2027
claims.reasoning: Confirmed in Bloomberg/Fortune's text; The Information's full body is paywalled and its timing details could not be independently confirmed, so this stays single-source and attributed rather than upgraded.

claims.text: Nvidia did not respond to requests for comment on the price increase
claims.reasoning: Stated directly in Bloomberg's reporting (via Fortune republication). No Nvidia blog post, newsroom release, or investor statement addressing pricing was found (checked blogs.nvidia.com / nvidianews.nvidia.com / investor.nvidia.com).

falsifier_notes: Cycle ran one adversarial-by-design verifier pass rather than a separate second falsifier pass, given the cycle time window (see budget note in the run report); the verifier's brief explicitly required tracing the lead (which named only Semafor) back to its origin rather than trusting it, and that redirection is what surfaced the Bloomberg/Information split. Findings: Semafor's own text credits Bloomberg by name ('Bloomberg reported') and was excluded as a source; no Nvidia statement, denial, or on-record comment exists anywhere; no outlet disputes that a price increase is happening (Reuters ran a brief noting it 'could not immediately verify the report' -- a hedge, not a contradiction, and Reuters is not cited as a source here for that reason). Neither Bloomberg's direct URL nor The Information's full paywalled body could be fetched directly; Bloomberg's content was corroborated via Fortune's same-byline republication, and The Information's headline/byline/lede were confirmed via search-result extracts rather than the full paywalled article -- flagged here for a complete audit trail.
